tagline: Link roadmap cards in Trello to engineering issues in Linear
metaTitle: Linear + Trello Integration: Trello Cards to Linear Issues
metaDescription: Keep your Trello roadmap honest. GAIA creates Linear issues from roadmap cards and moves each card once all its issues ship. See the setup steps.
intro:
Product teams that plan roadmaps in Trello and engineering teams that execute in Linear often struggle to keep both views in sync. A card representing a roadmap feature may spawn ten issues, but the card has no idea when those issues are completed. Product managers watch the board and have no signal that engineering has shipped the underlying work.

GAIA creates and maintains the link between cards and issues so product and engineering always share the same reality. When a card moves to In Development, GAIA creates the corresponding engineering issues. As those issues progress and complete, GAIA updates the card automatically. When the last issue ships, the card moves to Done.

This integration suits companies that want to keep using Trello for high-level roadmap planning — its visual simplicity and broad accessibility make it popular with non-technical stakeholders — while giving engineering the power of Linear for day-to-day sprint work.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Trello cards
useCases.description: When a card is moved to the Ready for Development list, GAIA breaks it into issues based on the card checklist items, assigns them to the relevant team, and attaches the card URL for reference.

useCases.title: Update card status from issue progress
useCases.description: As issues linked to a card progress, GAIA updates the card's checklist items and custom fields so product managers see a live progress indicator on the roadmap card without checking Linear.

useCases.title: Auto-move cards when all issues ship
useCases.description: When all issues linked to a card are marked Done, GAIA automatically moves the card to the Shipped list on the board, giving the roadmap an accurate picture of what has been delivered.

useCases.title: Attach sprint cycle info to roadmap cards
useCases.description: GAIA writes the target cycle to a card's label or custom field so product managers can see at a glance which sprint a feature is scheduled for without asking engineering.

useCases.title: Notify card members of issue blockers
useCases.description: When a linked issue moves to Blocked, GAIA adds a comment to the card summarizing the blocker so product owners can take cross-team action without waiting for standup.

howItWorks.step: Connect Trello and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Trello account and Linear workspace. Map boards to teams and define which lists correspond to which development stages.
Specify which list moves trigger issue creation, how checklist items map to issue titles, and which issue state changes should update the card.

howItWorks.step: Keep roadmap and sprint board aligned automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA handles every update between the two tools from that point. Product managers work on the roadmap board, engineers work in the sprint board, and both stay synchronized without anyone manually managing the connection.

faqs.question: Can one card be linked to multiple Linear issues?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is the typical use case. A single roadmap card often represents a feature that requires multiple engineering tasks. GAIA tracks all linked issues and rolls up their status to the card automatically.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with Trello Power-Ups?
faqs.answer: GAIA operates through the API and works alongside existing Power-Ups without conflict. It uses standard card fields, custom fields, and comments, so it is compatible with most popular Power-Up configurations.

faqs.question: What if we move a card back to a previous list?
faqs.answer: GAIA detects backward movement and can optionally reopen the corresponding issues or add a comment to notify the engineering team. You configure whether regressions should trigger automatic actions or just log a notification.
